text: εὐθύς, adj. (a) straight, of direction, as opposed to crooked (σκολιός); (b) met. upright.
note: The app's lemma εὐθύς is linked to Souter's adjective entry; Souter has a separate adverb entry immediately after it: "εὐθύς, adv. immediately: characteristic of Mk." (most NT occurrences are the adverb).

text: εὐθέως, immediately.
εὐδοκέω, I am well-pleased, c. acc. expressing with, Mt. xii 18, &c.; I think it good, am resolved (a characteristic word of Jewish Greek).

εὐδοκία, (a) good-will (good-pleasure), favour, feeling of complacency of God to man: ἄνθρωποι εὐδοκίας (Hebraistic), men with whom God is well-pleased, Lk. ii 14; (b) good-pleasure, satisfaction, happiness, delight of men, e. g. 2 Thess. i 11, though even in such passages there may be a latent reference to (divine) approval.
εὐλογέω, (lit. I speak well of, opp. I abuse, curse) I bless; εὐλογημένος, of a man, blessed (by God; contrast εὐλογητός): εὐλογῶν (or ἐν εὐλογίᾳ) εὐλογῶ (Hebraistic), I bless abundantly.
εὐλογία, blessing.
εὐλογητός (used only of God), blessed (as entitled to receive blessing from man).
εὔκοπος, easy.
εὐπρόσδεκτος, well-received, acceptable, welcome.
εὑρίσκω (reperio), I find, especially after searching; but in Phil. iii 9 possibly I surprise.
εὐχαριστέω, I give thanks: pass. 3 sing. is received with thanks, 2 Cor. i 11.
εὐσέβεια, piety (towards God), godliness.
εὐχαριστία, thankfulness, gratitude.
εὐφραίνω, I cheer, make glad: generally mid. or pass. I am glad; I make merry, revel, feast.
εὐσχήμων, (a) comely, seemly, decorous; (b) of honourable position (in society).

ἔχω, (a) tr. I hold, have, possess; ἔσχον, generally, I got, received, acquired, ἔσχηκα, I possessed; ἔχω τι κατά (εἰς), I have a ground of complaint against; ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν, to have (a child) in the womb; with double acc., the second being in the pred. (with or without εἰς), to have so and so as . . ., to regard so and so as (cf. Mk. xi 32); with obj. indicating time (cf. Fr. avoir) to be so and so days &c. old; (b) c. infin. I am able; (c) c. adv. equal to εἰμί with corresponding adjective; (d) intr. κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων, having a covering over the head, with head covered, 1 Cor. xi 4; (e) Mid. I am neighbouring, I am next to, e. g. Mk. i 38, τῇ ἐχομένῃ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ), next day, Lk. xiii 33, cf. Ac. xiii 44 (v.l.), &c.
note: The letter in '(e) Mid.' is faint on the image and could be read as (c); (e) follows the sequence (a)-(d). The breathing and accent on εἰς (twice) are small and hard to make out.

text: ἐχθρός, an enemy.
ἐφίστημι: in intr. tenses and passive, I come upon (suddenly or unexpectedly) and stand by: met. I press forward, 2 Tim. iv 2.

ἕως, (a) conj. until: followed by the indic. where a definite time in the past is indicated; with or without οὗ or ὅτου, and followed by the subjunctive aorist with, or without, ἂν or ἐάν, indicating an indefinite time, until . . . shall have, e. g. ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται, until all shall have happened, Mt. v 18; (b) prep. as far as, up to, as much as, until, both in local and temporal connexions, both with nouns in gen. and with adverbs (or prepositions).
ζάω, I live; ἑαυτῷ ζῆν, to be one’s own master.
ζῆλος (masc. and neut.), (a) eagerness, zeal, enthusiasm; (b) jealousy, rivalry.

ζωή, life, both of physical (present) and of spiritual (particularly future) existence; sometimes, e. g. Mk. x 17, = Hebrew ḥayyīm (a plural form) = all the days you are alive (nearer to βίος than ζωή), of a place in the New Age.
ζητέω (quaero), I seek, search for.
ζύμη, leaven, ferment, both lit. and met.
ζηλόω, (a) intr. I am jealous; (b) tr. I am jealous of, with acc. of a person; I am eager for, I am eager to possess, with acc. of a thing.
ζήτησις, questioning.
note: Headword print is damaged (the iota is broken), and the mark after it looks like a semicolon, probably a blemish for Souter's usual comma; transcribed as a comma.

text: ζήτημα (quaestio), a question, subject of inquiry.

ἤ, (a) or, both in rel. and interrog. clauses: in interrog. sentences we ought perhaps sometimes to accent ἦ (cf. εἰ) and regard simply as an interrogative particle, not to be translated; (b) than, sometimes almost otiose after πρίν; ἀλλ’ ἤ (Lk. xii 51, 2 Cor. i 13) should be ἄλλ’ ἤ (i. e. ἄλλο ἤ), nothing but; ἢ γάρ in Lk. xviii 14 (v.l.) is corrupt.
note: Breathings and accents on the small Greek forms are faint: headword read as ἤ, 'accent ἦ' (circumflex), '(cf. εἰ)' (breathing only), and 'ἢ γάρ' (grave).

text: ἤδη, already; now at length, now after all this waiting Rom. i 10.
ἡγέομαι, (a) I lead: ὁ ἡγούμενος (as subst.), the leader; (b) (cf. duco) I think, I am of opinion.
ἥκω, I have come, but other tenses are translated as if the present meant I come.
ζῷον, an animal.
ἡγεμών (praeses, a very wide word), a (Roman) governor.
ζωοποιέω, I make that which was dead to live.

ἡμέρα (dies), a day, the period from sunrise to sunset; (ἡ) ἡμέρα κρίσεως, ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη, ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου, the judgement day, coinciding with the end of the world, according to late Jewish belief; τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ, &c., on the third day, after two days, so διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν, Mt. xxvi 61, &c.; νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, through night as well as day; νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας, by night as well as day, imply merely before dawn as well as during the day; (τὸ) καθ’ ἡμέραν, day by day, each day; πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας (vernacular phrase), perpetually, Mt. xxviii 20.
note: In 'πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας' the print of πάσας is blurred (could be misread as πάσης); also the final '20' is faint.

text: ἥλιος, the sun; μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον, equivalent to stone-blind, Ac. xiii 11.

θάνατος, death, physical or spiritual; θάνατοι appears to mean risks to life, 2 Cor. xi 23; ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος (ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος), the death of the spiritual part in man, practically annihilation of personality.

θάλασσα, (a) the sea, in contrast to the land (γῆ): τὸ πέλαγος τῆς θαλάσσης (tautol.), the depth of the sea, Mt. xviii 6; (b) a particular sea or lake, e. g. the sea of Galilee (Tiberias), the Red Sea.
θέλω, (a) intr. I will; οὐ θέλω, I refuse; θέλειν ἐν, to fix one’s will on, to stick resolutely to, Col. ii 18; followed by subj. with, or without, ἵνα, I will that; (b) tr. I wish, desire.
θέλημα, an act of will, will; plur. wishes, desires; τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, the will of God, sometimes as a will to be recognized, sometimes as a will to be obeyed.
θαυμάζω, (a) intr. I wonder; cognate acc. θαυμάζειν θαῦμα μέγα, Rev. xvii 6, to wonder very greatly; (b) tr. I wonder at, admire.
θεάομαι (specto), I behold.
θεμέλιος (properly an adj. belonging to the foundation, with λίθος understood), a foundation stone; plur. neut. θεμέλια is used, Ac. xvi 26.
θάπτω, I bury.
θανατόω, I put to death.

θεός, (a) a god or goddess, John x 34, 35, Ac. vii 40, xiv 11, xix 26, 37, 1 Cor. viii 5, Gal. iv 8; (b) the god. The word is an appellative. The Christian, like the Jew and many pagans, avoided naming his God, and referred to him as the god.
θεωρέω (specto), I behold, look at.
θεραπεύω, I care for, attend, serve, treat, especially of a physician; hence I heal, sometimes with ἀπό, of.
θερίζω, I reap.
θερισμός, reaping, harvest.
θεμελιόω, I found, lit. and met.
θρόνος, a (king’s) throne, seat.
θηρίον, properly a wild beast, hence any animal.
θλῖψις, persecution, affliction, distress.
θησαυρός, a store-house for precious things; hence a treasure, a store.
θρίξ, a hair; plur. hair.
θλίβω, (a) I make narrow (strictly by pressure), Mt. vii 14; I press upon, Mk. iii 9; (b) I persecute, press hard.
θνῄσκω, I am dying: perf. τέθνηκα, I am dead; τεθνηκώς, dead.
θησαυρίζω, I store up, I treasure up, I save.
θνητός, mortal.
θύρα, (a) a door; (b) met. an opportunity, Ac. xiv 27, 1 Cor. xvi 9, &c.
θυγάτηρ, a daughter; hence (Hebraistic?), of any female descendant, however far removed, Lk. i 5, xiii 16; even of one unrelated, my young lady, Mk. v 34, &c.
θυσία, abstr. and concr., sacrifice; a sacrifice.
θυσιαστήριον, an altar (for sacrifice).
θυμός, an outburst of passion, wrath.
θύω, I sacrifice, generally an animal; hence I kill.
θυμίαμα, incense.

ἴδιος (ἵδιος) (proprius), one’s own, belonging to one, private, personal: οἱ ἴδιοι, one’s own people, one’s own family, John i 11; ὁ ἴδιος, possibly his own (son), Ac. xx 28; τὰ ἴδια, one’s own home, one’s own property, John i 11, &c.; ἰδίᾳ, κατ’ ἰδίαν (καθ’ ἰδίαν) (possibly sc. ὁδόν), privately, apart, in private, by oneself, individually.
note: Breathing on the parenthetical variant is small: read as rough (ἵδιος), smooth on the headword.

text: ἰάομαι, I heal, generally of physical, sometimes of spiritual, disease.
ἱερός, sacred.
ἱερεύς, a priest, one who offers sacrifice to a god (in Jewish and pagan religions; of Christians only metaphorically).

ἱκανός, (a) considerable, sufficient, of number, quantity, time: ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων (v. l. ἱκανοῦ), already for a long time, Lk. xxiii 8 (cf. viii 27), ἐφ’ ἱκανόν, for a sufficiently long time, Ac. xx 11; ἱκανόν ἐστιν, enough of this subject, Lk. xxii 38 (cf. 2 Cor. ii 6); τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιεῖν τινι (satis facere alicui), to satisfy one, to give him no ground of complaint, Mk. xv 15, τὸ ἱκανὸν λαμβάνω (satis accipio), I get surety (security), Ac. xvii 9; (b) of persons, sufficiently strong (good, &c.), worthy, suitable, with various constructions.

ἵνα, (A) in statements: (a) indicating purpose, in order that; (b) indicating a command or wish, Mk. v 23, vi 25, x 35, 51, John xvii 24, 1 Cor. vii 29, 2 Cor. viii 7, Gal. ii 10, Eph. v 33; (c) indicating consequence, so that, e. g. Rom. xi 11; (d) a mere introduction to a noun clause, that, e. g. John xvii 3; (B) in interrogations: ἵνα τί (ut quid), why? wherefore?
ἱμάτιον, a long flowing outer garment.
ἵππος, a horse.

ἱστάνω (form appearing first in 3rd cent. B.C.), ἵστημι, (a) tr. in tenses of the active mood (including new perf. -έστακα), except 2 aor. and perf. (form ἕστηκα) and plup., I make to stand, I set up: I weigh (pay), Mt. xxvi 15; (b) intr. in 2 aor. and perf. (form ἕστηκα) and plup., also mid. and pass., I am set up, I am made to stand, I stand, I take an erect position, I stand firm: = ἀντιστῆναι, Eph. vi 13.
note: Souter's combined entry for ἱστάνω and ἵστημι.

text: ἰσχυρός, strong (originally and generally of physical strength); powerful.

ἰσχύω, I have strength, I am strong, I am in full health and vigour (opp. κακῶς ἔχω) Mt. ix 12; and so I am able, sometimes followed by the inf. or εἰς c. acc. to indicate the purpose for which the strength is used, e. g. Mt. xxvi 40, v 13; c. acc. adverbially, qualifying the strength, τι ἰσχύει, has any validity (value), Gal. v 6, cf. Heb. ix 17, πάντα ἰσχύω, I have all strength (power), Phil. iv 13, πολὺ ἰσχύει, has great power, James v 16.
ἰσχύς, strength (absolutely).
ἰχθύς, a fish.

καθαρίζω (alternative spelling καθερίζω, perhaps = καθαιρίζω, but it occurs only in augmented and reduplicated forms and has been otherwise explained) (purgo), I make clean, literally, ceremonially, or spiritually, according to context, ἀπό c. gen. being sometimes added, of the dirt removed.
καθαρός (purus), clean, pure, unstained, either literally or ceremonially or spiritually; καθαρὸς ἀπό, unstained by.
καθάπερ (i. e. καθ’ ἅπερ, according to which things), even as.
note: The apostrophe after καθ is faint or missing on the image (cf. the καθά entry just above, which prints καθ’ ἅ); transcribed as καθ’.

text: καθαρισμός, cleansing, purifying, purification, literal, ceremonial, or moral.
καί, and; sometimes modifying a following word, even.
καθώς, according to the manner in which, in the degree that, as.
κάθημαι, I am seated, I sit: καθήμενος, seated, sitting.
καθίζω, (a) tr. I make to sit, I set; (b) intr. aor. I sat down.
καινός (recens), fresh, new.
καθεύδω, I am sleeping (asleep), I sleep.
καθίστημι, καθιστάνω, in the tr. tenses (see ἵστημι), I set, establish, appoint, constitute, make; I conduct, Ac. xvii 15: καθίσταται, shows itself, acts its part, James iii 6.
καιρός, fitting season, season, opportunity, occasion, time: πρὸς καιρόν, for a time.
κακός, bad, evil, in the widest sense.
καίω, tr. I ignite, I light, I burn, lit. and met.
κακία, (a) evil (i. e. trouble, labour, misfortune), Mt. vi 34; (b) wickedness, Ac. viii 22; (c) vicious disposition, malice, spite.

καρδία (Lat. cor, Hebr. lēb, lēbab), (A) lit. the heart, as an organ of the body; (B) mind covers the non-physical sense best: (a) personality, character, inner life (illa uis qua cogitationes fiunt, Augustine, De nat. et orig. animae iv 6 § 7), e. g. 1 Cor. xiv 25, 1 Pet. i 22; (b) emotional state, e. g. Rom. ix 2; (c) mind, intellect, e. g. Rom. i 21; (d) will, volition, intention, e. g. Rom. ii 5.
note: Targets list this under page 130, but the entry is printed on page 131 (page 130 ends at καπηλεύω).

text: καλέω, (a) I call, summon, invite; (b) I call, name: ἐπί, after, Lk. i 59.
καλός (honestus), beautiful, as an outward sign of the inward good, noble, honourable character; good, worthy, honourable, noble, and seen to be so.

καλῶς, well, nobly, honourably; in a good place, James ii 3: compar. κάλλιον; καλῶς ποιήσεις, especially with aor. participle, is idiomatic for please, 3 John 6, cf. Ac. x 33, Phil. iv 14, 2 Pet. i 19.
κακῶς, badly, evilly: κακῶς ἔχω, see ἔχω.
καπνός, smoke.
note: Targets list this under page 130, but the entry is printed at the top of page 131.

text: κάλαμος, a reed; a reed-pen, 3 John 13.
